evaluation-system.goal: Evaluate agent session quality, calibrate criteria, detect drift, patrol integrity, extract strategies
evaluation-system.summary: Project-app evaluation system with five lanes. Current owner focus is now narrowed to the aftermath trigger-leak audit: live 72h workflow_runs show 2625 done vs 1301 missing-sessionId escalations and 50 interrupted runs, while the previously observed review-failed lane is currently at zero. Keep pipeline-health active around routing leakage first, then resume secondary lanes once the leak source is isolated.

pipeline-health.goal: Monitor evaluation pipeline: is aftermath keeping up? Are there gaps? Is LLM lane useful?
pipeline-health.summary: Live evidence still shows the lane is active and leaky, but the shape is narrower than the prior check. Last 72h workflow_runs for evaluator-aftermath: 2625 done, 1301 escalated with result_reason="evaluator-aftermath requires a sessionId", 0 evaluator review-failed escalations, and 50 interrupted runs. Last 24h shows 85 missing-sessionId escalations, 0 review-failed escalations, and 44 interrupted runs. Among current missing-sessionId escalations, 84/85 still carry an embedded ## Trigger Event while 1/85 uses the generic periodic aftermath task text with no parent linkage, so routing/extraction leakage remains the dominant actionable problem.

aftermath-trigger-leak-audit.goal: Identify why evaluator-aftermath still receives triggers without a concrete sessionId and package the smallest fix or escalation.
acceptance: Quantifies which trigger/event shapes are producing the missing-sessionId escalations now.
Identifies the exact upstream emitter or dispatch path responsible for the leak.
Packages the next action as either a local implementation task or a concrete escalation with evidence.

latest_evidence.signal: The leak is still active and now better scoped. In the last 24h, 84 of 85 missing-sessionId escalations still embed a full ## Trigger Event whose data.sessionId should be parseable by evaluator-aftermath, which keeps evaluator-side trigger extraction/routing the primary suspect. One fresh escalation still uses the generic periodic aftermath task text with no parentSessionId, parentWorkflowRunId, or projectId, so the audit should also trace whether any stale legacy dispatcher still emits bare aftermath work.

aftermath-reviewer-runtime-failures.goal: Reduce evaluator review-failed escalations caused by unavailable evaluator runtime dependencies or provider capacity.
acceptance: Classifies the current failure modes (for example 429 no deployment, 401 token expired, missing python/command assumptions) with concrete session evidence.
Separates evaluator-owned prompt/workflow fixes from runtime-owner issues.
Leaves a concrete repair or escalation task instead of a generic complaint.

latest_evidence.signal: The previously observed evaluator review-failed escalations are not present in the current 24h or 72h window, so this lane is no longer the best use of active attention. Keep it parked in backlog and resume if review-failed escalations recur; current pipeline-health work should stay focused on the missing-sessionId leak, with interrupted runs noted separately as restart noise unless they become the primary failure mode.

criteria-and-calibration.goal: Maintain scoring criteria, calibrate against human reviews, version criteria changes
criteria-and-calibration.summary: Criteria at v1. Calibration scaffolding exists but criteria/calibration is empty and the prior summary references only 2026-04-29 placeholder stubs. A fresh 2026-06 disagreement sample is needed before criteria changes are credible.

seed-fresh-calibration-batch.goal: Build a fresh calibration baseline from current 2026-06 evaluations instead of relying on placeholder stubs.
acceptance: Samples recent sessions with disagreement or false-good risk from the live DB.
Records at least one real calibration artifact under criteria/calibration or explains why a different durable location is better.
Updates task-tree context with what the new sample says about criteria drift.
